description: I am a Year 12 student from the UK studying maths, physics and further maths.
summary:
I developed an educational, interactive website exploring the Voyager program. The website features the history of the voyager program, compares the paths and purposes of Voyager 1 and 2, explores their accomplishments, including visiting planets and escaping the heliopause, explores the Golden Record and more.

It addresses the challenge as it is focused on being interactive, in order to capture the interest of the user, and teaches the user about the Voyager program, which much of the population are unaware of.

It is important as I recently realised the lack of awareness of the Voyager program among other students studying physics. This was very surprising to me as I found the program very interesting and learnt about it at a young age. Therefore, I believe it is important to bring awareness to missions and space programs, such as the Voyager program, to inspire young people, like how I was, by showing the amazing accomplishments of humanity, demonstrated by the Voyagers.
details:
My project is an educational website filled with interactive components that aim to engage the user and create an interest in space and space missions.

I used HTML, CSS and JavaScript to build the website. ChatGPT was used to help with coding.

Creative ideas include a built in SoundCloud music player that allows the user to listen to the Golden Record from within the website. I also incorporated NASA Eyes into the website, allowing the user to explore the voyagers' current positions in relation to the Earth. There is also a countdown (which updates every second), until Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth.

Throughout the website I was always thinking of ways to let the user interact and make it engaging which was my main goal.

All image sources are noted on the website.
